note: THE INVITE GATE BECOMES A SWITCH, AND THE SWITCH IS SET TO OFF.
Tyler is opening the beta (2026-08-23). Deleting b457's gate was the
wrong move: twenty codes are already in people's hands, 'one code = one
account' is a property several things assume, and the beta may be
re-closed at any time. So the gate becomes CONDITIONAL on a row rather
than absent, and re-closing is ONE statement:
update public.hr_settings set value = 'on' where key = 'beta_gate';
Adds public.hr_settings (RLS on, ZERO policies, zero client grants, a
per-key domain CHECK so beta_gate can only ever be 'on'/'off') seeded
beta_gate='off' ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING - a re-apply must never silently
re-open a beta somebody closed. Adds hr_beta_gate_is_open() (FAIL
CLOSED: anything it cannot prove is 'off' reads as the closed beta) and
hr_beta_signup_message() (the new copy layer; hr_beta_gate_message is
deliberately NOT restated - two files owning one `case` is a failure
this repo has already paid for).
RESTATES three b457 bodies: hr_beta_gate_reason (ONE line - the
invite_required arm now consults the switch), hr_signup_gate (adds a
per-IP codeless-signup ACCOUNT brake, 10/day, live ONLY while the gate
is open) and hr_beta_gate_on_auth_user (adds ONE arm: codeless + gate
open => allowed, journalled outcome='open'). The trigger REGISTRATION,
the operator/admin bypasses, hr_beta_code_norm's 64-char bound, the
append-only journal and claim_beta_invite's revoked grant are untouched.
RULING, asserted in both directions: a code that IS supplied is still
validated and consumed in EVERY mode - a bogus code refuses even with
the gate open, so a typo cannot silently succeed while the player's real
code sits unspent, beta_invites.used_by keeps meaning something, one
code stays one account, and the enumeration signal survives.
MUST run AFTER 2026-08-23-beta-invite-gate.sql (its §0 fails closed
without hr_beta_gate_reason / hr_signup_gate / hr_beta_code_norm / the
attached trigger) and after 2026-08-11-player-state.sql (hr_rate_ok /
hr_rate_over / hr_rate_sample_weight / hr_record_rejection). Touches
none of the graded bodies (hr_apply / hr_state_of / hr_perks_of /
hr_rate_gate / hr_assert_grant_hygiene) so it is on no derivation chain.
NO edge redeploy - nothing in the hr-accrue import graph.
Self-check (rolled-back subtransactions, net-zero, and it FORCES
enforcement with hearthrise.invite_gate_force so the postgres bypass
cannot wave the probe through): the switch flips both ways; gate ON
reproduces b457's whole refusal set including the select-into-NULL
fail-open guard; all four spellings of 'no code' (absent key, '', '   ',
null) are accepted with the gate off; a bogus code still refuses; the
10/day/IP brake bites WITH a different-IP control and does not touch a
code-bearing signup; every b457 player-facing sentence survives the
message delegation. Trigger checks 8-11 need auth.users.raw_user_meta_data
and run on the real database only - tests/open-beta.mjs adds that column
to the PGlite fixture and drives them there.
OPS (not database state, listed in §9): email confirmations ON, auth
rate limits, the before-user-created hook still registered (the account
brake lives in the hook and CANNOT live in the trigger - no client IP
exists there), anonymous sign-ins OFF.
Reversibility: the one-line UPDATE above, or re-apply
2026-08-23-beta-invite-gate.sql to restore the three bodies verbatim.
Graded by tests/open-beta.mjs + tests/beta-invite-gate.mjs.
